GSE67203.note: (GEO summary read) The only GEO series found with ADULT exposure followed by a drug-free interval in mammalian brain: rats given fluoxetine 12 mg/kg at PND 67-88, hippocampus profiled 'long-term' afterwards. But only 4 samples (2 fluoxetine, 2 vehicle; pooled or not is not stated in the summary) - no usable statistics. Hippocampus, not a sexual-function region.

GSE316091.note: (GEO summary read) The only antipsychotic post-treatment dataset: mouse cortex snRNA-seq 9 weeks after adolescent risperidone. 4 samples (2 risperidone, 2 saline). Adolescent exposure, cortex only; shows the design is feasible.

GSE111362.note: (GEO summary read; sample titles read) Perinatal paroxetine (dams 10 mg/kg/day), offspring hippocampus and amygdala arrays at P7/P14/P21, n=78. Early-life exposure, readout in juveniles not adults. The 'withdraw' keyword refers to neonatal withdrawal in the background text, not a washout arm.

GSE270730.note: (GEO summary read) Postnatal fluoxetine, rat medial prefrontal cortex profiled in adulthood (4 vs 4 arrays). Early-life exposure with adult readout. No PMID linked.

GSE270731.note: (title only, summary not hand-read; sister series of GSE270730) Juvenile fluoxetine, rat mPFC in adulthood, 8 arrays.

GSE42940.note: (title only, summary not hand-read) Postnatal fluoxetine, rat hippocampus, 8 arrays; early-life exposure.

GSE189653.note: (GEO summary read) Mouse whole brain at P120 after fluoxetine P3-P21 via milk, wild-type and Arid1b-het, RNA-seq. Roughly 100 drug-free days after early-life SSRI; the wild-type fluoxetine vs vehicle arm is the relevant contrast.

GSE203343.note: (title only, summary not hand-read; same project as GSE189653) Prefrontal cortex at P120 after early fluoxetine, 16 samples.

GSE111491.note: (GEO summary read) Prenatal (in utero) fluoxetine, adult mouse brain, 4 arrays only.

GSE308723.note: (GEO summary read) Zebrafish embryos exposed to citalopram 2-24 hpf, expression assessed later: explicitly about persistence after transient exposure. Fish embryo, whole organism; weak translational relevance.

GSE141144.note: (GEO summary read) Zebrafish early-life fluoxetine, telencephalon and hypothalamus in larvae and adults, n=6 per group. 'Withdrawn' refers to transgenerational background. Fish.

_gap_statement: SENSORY GANGLIA / SPINAL CORD / GENITAL TISSUE: no GEO series profiles dorsal root ganglia, sensory neurons, spinal cord, pudendal/pelvic nerve, penis, clitoris or genital skin after any of the 17 drugs. The single keyword hit (GSE255683) is an ALS spinal-cord study, not a drug study. The nearest thing is fetal rat anogenital tissue during in-utero finasteride (GSE122494). For a syndrome whose hallmark is genital numbness this is the central gap.

ADULT WASHOUT DESIGNS: across all drugs, GEO holds one adult treat-then-stop dataset in mammalian brain (GSE67203, fluoxetine, rat hippocampus, 4 samples). Everything else flagged 'persistent' is early-life (perinatal / postnatal / adolescent) exposure read out later.

ANTIPSYCHOTIC WASHOUT: none in adults. One adolescent-exposure dataset (GSE316091, risperidone, mouse cortex, 2 vs 2). Nothing for olanzapine, quetiapine, aripiprazole, haloperidol or clozapine after discontinuation.
MIRTAZAPINE: no in-vivo dataset at all and no washout dataset; only a 48 h cortical-neuron culture (GSE63005) and one-replicate screen entries (GSE110256).

FINASTERIDE / DUTASTERIDE: prostate (mostly cancer or BPH) and toxicogenomic liver/kidney only. No brain, nerve or penile tissue in GEO, no withdrawal arm, and no post-finasteride-syndrome patient dataset: the published patient penile-skin expression study (PMID 34247957, returned by PubMed in this session) was not found in GEO by any query here.
ISOTRETINOIN: toxicogenomic, teratogenicity (iPSC/embryoid) and skin/sebocyte series only; no neural or genital tissue in vivo, no post-treatment design.
HUMAN TISSUE FROM AFFECTED PATIENTS (PSSD, PFS, post-retinoid): none in GEO for any tissue.

THE MOST RELEVANT DATASETS ARE NOT IN GEO: the rat paroxetine treatment-and-withdrawal RNA-seq of hypothalamus and nucleus accumbens (Giatti et al., Mol Neurobiol 2025, PMID 39495228) and the matching finasteride study of hypothalamus and hippocampus (Giatti et al., J Endocrinol Invest 2024, PMID 38493246) were searched for in GEO (db=gds), BioProject and SRA and not found. Their per-sample normalised counts are, however, in the journal supplementary tables; these are what REANALYSIS.md uses. Raw reads appear not to be public (the finasteride paper says data are available on request).

EPIGENOMIC DATA: methylation / chromatin datasets exist only on-treatment (e.g. fluoxetine H3K27ac GSE193040, haloperidol GSE67755, olanzapine methylation GSE52615, human placental methylation after maternal SSRI GSE203396). None tests whether an epigenetic mark outlasts the drug in an adult.
